newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Fast crush pace weighs on basis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Fast crush pace weighs on basis.

text.p: Soymeal basis levels were steady to lower on Friday as the recent fast crush pace weighed on nearby values, dealers said.
"There is plenty of meal in the system," one dealer said.
They noted, however, that meal for early July delivery was up to $7.00 per ton more expensive amid growing concern about supply tightness for old crop soybeans.

"I think most (crushers) are covered for June (beans) but there is nervousness about what it is going to take to buy beans in July," one dealer said, noting some crushers still needed to secure soybean supplies to crush in July.

Dealers said the nearby rail soymeal levels for Decatur, Ill., were around $13.00 per ton over CBOT July while for late June the price rose to $18.00 per ton over CBOT July. For July the price was even stronger at about $20.00 over CBOT July.
The National Oilseed Processors Association reported Thursday that the crush for the week to June 4 was a strong 25.63 million bushels, up from 25.46 million a week earlier.
